summary.en: Track a front cursor and a rear cursor to serve arrivals in FIFO order.
summary.bn: Front ও rear দিয়ে আসার ক্রমে কিউ থেকে মান বের করো।

notes: Programs use C17 with explicit bounds and ownership checks.

examples.title: Enqueue at rear and dequeue at front
examples.explanationHtml: Twelve leaves before twenty-four. Front advances independently of rear.

examples.title: Observe wasted prefix cells
examples.explanationHtml: Two cells become unused at the front, but rear remains four, so five is refused.

examples.title: Reach the empty linear state
examples.explanationHtml: Empty removal changes neither cursor; after removing nine, both cursors equal one.

practice.title: Process a linear queue stream
practice.statementHtml: Read 0..16 commands after their count. Zero requests dequeue; other integers enqueue into four linear cells. Print the prompt, removal or rejection messages, then Items: and Indices: front rear as in the example.
hints: Rear denotes the next unused physical cell.

practice.title: Reuse storage only after draining
practice.statementHtml: Use the linear-queue stream and output format. Reset both cursors to zero after a successful removal empties the queue.
hints: A reset is safe only when no live value remains.

practice.title: Report waiting count without compaction
practice.statementHtml: Use the linear-queue command rules and messages. Before the final Items: and Indices: lines, print Waiting: and the live count.
hints: The live interval length is rear minus front.

practice.title: Count writes refused at the linear boundary
practice.statementHtml: Use the linear command format and prompt. Count refused enqueue requests without printing individual No rear space messages. Keep removal/empty messages, then print Refused: count before the usual Items: and Indices: lines.
hints: A freed prefix does not lower rear.

quiz.prompt: Which cursor identifies the next linear queue removal?
quiz.explanation: Front points to the oldest live entry.

quiz.prompt: What is the empty condition with next-write rear?
quiz.explanation: The half-open live interval has length zero.

quiz.prompt: Why can rear reach capacity while front is positive?
options: Removals advance front without lowering rear
quiz.explanation: The freed prefix is outside the remaining write range.

quiz.prompt: How expensive is dequeuing without shifting?
quiz.explanation: Only one read and a cursor update are needed.

quiz.prompt: When can both cursors safely reset to zero?
options: When the live queue is empty
quiz.explanation: A reset while values remain would lose their live interval.
FIFO preserves arrival order, not numerical order.

quiz.prompt: What does compacting live values reclaim?
quiz.explanation: Compaction shifts the remaining suffix to index zero.

quiz.prompt: Which cell is next after a linear queue starts with two waiting values?
quiz.explanation: FIFO removes the oldest queued value.

quiz.prompt: How many live values lie between front=2 and rear=4?
quiz.explanation: Rear is the first unused position.

quiz.prompt: Does rear=4 allow another insertion in a four-cell linear queue?
quiz.explanation: The linear implementation cannot reuse the prefix.

keyPoints.bn: কিউতে যে আগে আসে, সে আগে বের হয়।

keyPoints.en: Rear identifies the next unused linear cell.
keyPoints.bn: Linear কিউতে rear পরের অব্যবহৃত ঘর দেখায়।

keyPoints.en: An empty linear queue has equal front and rear cursors.
keyPoints.bn: Front ও rear সমান হলে linear কিউ খালি।

keyPoints.en: Advancing front does not move the remaining values.
keyPoints.bn: Front বাড়ালে বাকি মানগুলো সরাতে হয় না।

keyPoints.en: A linear queue can waste freed prefix cells.
keyPoints.bn: Linear কিউয়ের সামনের খালি ঘর অব্যবহৃত থাকতে পারে।

examQuestions.question: Trace enqueue 3, enqueue 7, dequeue, enqueue 9 from empty using next-write rear.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The live states are [3], [3,7], [7], [7,9]. Final front is one, rear is three and live size is two. Physical cells one and two hold the final values.

examQuestions.question: A linear queue array starts at byte 2000 with four-byte cells. front=2 and rear=4. Find the front address and live count.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The next removal reads index two, whose address is 2000+2*4=2008. The live count is rear-front=2. Rear points to the next write location, not a live element.

examQuestions.question: After filling four linear cells and removing three values, why can enqueue still fail? Give two remedies.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Rear is still four and cannot advance within the array, although only one value remains. Moving the live suffix to the beginning reclaims space in O(n) time. Circular indexing reuses the prefix with O(1) operations. Resetting both indices helps only after the queue becomes completely empty.
